 FAA issues ground stop for all flights due to ‘extraordinary circumstances’ 
 4:20
 Ad Feedback 
 What's happening now
 • Ground stop: All flights in the United States are grounded until further notice, “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the Federal Aviation Administration said. 
 • Cause not yet known: The reason for the ground stop was not immediately clear, but an FAA spokesperson said there is a communications problem impacting Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which handle flights going across the country.
 • Rare instance: The last time there was a nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down. Prior to that, the last nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11, 2001, attacks.

 Preliminary reports indicate this is not a cyberattack, law enforcement sources say
 By Evan Perez and Hannah Rabinowitz 
 Preliminary reports indicate this is not a cyberattack, according to two law enforcement officials.
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:30 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Ground stop followed a communication issue, Duffy says
 By Pete Muntean 
 The FAA issued the ground stop “following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said in a social media post. “FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”
 Read more 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:31 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 Nationwide ground stops are rare
 By Aaron Cooper and Pete Muntean 
 Airplanes are seen on the tarmac at Logan Airport in Boston during a nationwide ground stop on Friday. 
 WBZ 
 The last time there was a nationwide ground stop was in January 2023, when a pilot notification system went down.
 Prior to that, the last nationwide ground stop was issued after the September 11, 2001, attacks.
 Read more 
 Updated Nov 13, 2026, 4:28 PM ET 
 Published Nov 13, 2026, 4:18 PM ET 
 Link Copied!
 FAA issues nationwide ground stop for all flights
 By Pete Muntean and Aaron Cooper 
 All flights in the United States are grounded until further notice, “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.
 The cause of the ground stop was not immediately clear, but an FAA spokesperson says there is a communications problem impacting Air Route Traffic Control Centers, which handle flights going across the country.
 “Traffic should remain ground stopped until further notice,” the FAA said in an advisory. “International flights will be managed on a case by case basis.”
